source.title: Robustness of Probabilistic Models to Low-Quality Data: A Multi-Perspective Analysis

record.tranche_reason: The study reports results about generalization under training-data corruption, but does not test the specific behaviors named in V1–V8. Its random target corruption is not the fixed random-label memorization test in V1; its batch-size measurements concern gradient or loss stability, not the large-batch generalization gap in V5; and its gradient measurements are not the sharpness measure in V7.
record.gate_note: The study varies training-data corruption and reports held-out metrics, training metrics, and gradient measurements. These do not directly test a listed version: the study does not test random-label memorization, width past interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected generalization, optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects on held-out performance, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study measures robustness to dynamically regenerated training-data corruption, not any V1–V8 intervention or comparison. It does not establish near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels for V1. Batch sizes change alongside corruption and training duration, or only during checkpoint measurements, so they do not test V5. Gradient coherence and loss variability do not measure V7 sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors conclude that autoregressive models and large-scale classifiers tolerate substantial corruption, whereas class-conditional diffusion models lose image-label consistency. They attribute these differences to conditioning-information richness and absolute correct information, proposing gradient aggregation as the mechanism. These are the authors' interpretations; the printed SNR results do not consistently substantiate their claimed improvement with batch size.
record.recipe_differences: Studies tolerance to added random or structured training-data corruption across language models, classifiers, and diffusion models; does not perform the listed memorization/generalization interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset scale and corruption structure change reported classifier outcomes; the authors report substantially worse classifier accuracy under systematic structured noise than under unstructured random noise at the same stated ratio. Batch-size conditions change measured gradient SNR and loss variability, not reported held-out performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the stated fixed training budget, GPT-2 training NLL rises from 2.7369 to 7.6048 while clean validation NLL rises from 2.8650 to 3.6525 at the highest corruption ratio.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GPT-2 retains useful clean-distribution prediction under substantial dynamic target corruption without closely fitting the noisy training targets.

fits_no_version.finding: Random label corruption reduces accuracy on CIFAR and ImageNet subsets; full ImageNet accuracy changes from 73.784% to 74.778% with increased training compute. Subset recipes also adjust batch sizes and duration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Robustness to dynamic random label corruption varies across the tested datasets and training recipes; these results suggest a role for scale without isolating it from all other differences.

fits_no_version.finding: At 50% effective corruption, systematic label shifts yield 40.72% CIFAR-10 and 33.39% CIFAR-100 accuracy, versus 85.35% and 61.65% with random incorrect labels. Clean baselines also differ between runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested systematic label errors damage classifier accuracy substantially more than random incorrect labels at the highest tested corruption rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Clean embedding gradients have mean cosine similarity +0.52 at initialization. Larger measurement batches reduce checkpoint loss variability; the printed SNR values contain internal inconsistencies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sample aggregation reduces measured loss variability in these checkpoint evaluations; these statistics do not establish a batch-size effect on held-out generalization.

record.problems: The study reports no uncertainty intervals for the extracted table outcomes. Its main corruption experiments add random or structured errors rather than testing arbitrary fixed-label memorization. The gradient coherence analysis is at initialization and concerns the token embedding layer; the loss-stability analysis explicitly is not a generalization measurement. Authors note scope limits including no systematic comparison of correlated-noise forms and no very large-scale diffusion experiments.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining Table 4 gradient-coherence entries (corrupt-vs-corrupt and clean-vs-corrupt means and ranges), aggregate clean/noise gradient magnitudes, and Table 11 clean-model loss statistics were omitted to stay within 60 rows and because they are training-dynamics measurements rather than a listed version's behavior. Main accuracy and GPT-2 train/validation outcomes, plus representative gradient and noisy-checkpoint batch-size outcomes, were retained.

untested.parts: Coexistence of near-perfect fixed-random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same recipe; chance held-out accuracy with random labels. Corruption here is regenerated dynamically and retains substantial correct supervision.
Width beyond the zero-training-error threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Held-out performance across batch sizes with corruption and epoch budgets controlled, and recovery through recipe adaptations. Reported convergence interventions do not supply this comparison.
Effects of adding or removing dropout, including dependence on dataset size, dropout strength, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and ranking against norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All rows retain versions=['none']; cannot_determine refers to V1–V8, not unreadable outcomes. Corruption ratios denote r, with effective error rate r/(1+r): 100:100 means 50%, not fully randomized labels. Missing is empty because omitted diffusion, sequence-to-sequence, and fixed-budget classifier results do not test a listed version. The supplied text identifies itself as a preprint and does not substantiate the record's ICLR peer-review designation.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fit fixed random labels or compare held-out accuracy on natural labels with held-out performance on random labels.
No width sweep past the zero-training-error threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
Batch size is adjusted or varied to study training stability and gradient statistics; no comparison of held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measure or comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.
